The psalmist confesses 'my folly is not hidden from you' (Ps 38:5; 69:5), linking it to guilt and spiritual exposure. Nearly every occurrence ties to the kesil or ewil — the obstinate fool who refuses correction."

Spanish 'necedad,' French 'folie,' and German 'Torheit' all capture the moral weight. Proverbs 22:15 declares it 'bound up in the heart of a child,' removable on...
    Existing Spanish translations: La-necedad, Necedad, en-necedad-su, necedad, necedad-de, su-necedad, y-necedad, y-necedad-de
